top_choice_rationale: P001 (MacDonald, Bistritzer, Jarillo-Herrero) pairs a quantitative 2011 prediction of flat bands at a magic twist angle with the 2018 discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states, reproduced by many independent laboratories and across several moire platforms. That robustness against twist-angle disorder and sample variation is, from a materials perspective, the best evidence of maturity, and the citation claims no pairing mechanism. The remaining weaknesses are the field's youth and the omission of Yuan Cao and earlier twisted-bilayer theorists, which the three-name limit forces. I still prefer P002 (Katori, Ye) to no award: it has a clean idea-plus-realisation split and 20 years of confirmation, though it is closer to a measurement capability than a discovery and follows the 2005 and 2012 metrology prizes.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; no documented connection to MacDonald, Bistritzer, Jarillo-Herrero, Katori or Ye. Chalmers colleague Goran Johansson is a co-member but not a candidate.
